scope: Independent screenshot UX critique for a prototype discussion.

findings.observation: The board uses date-ordered release cards with workflow states, pending counts, PT labels, and small approval icons.
findings.consequence: Reviewers must interpret small icons and raw timestamps before identifying pending work.
findings.next_action: Keep chronological cards. Display readable dates, explicit pending roles, and one clear reason requiring attention.

findings.observation: Release metadata precedes many compliance cards, including successful checks.
findings.consequence: Compliance cards occupy substantial space before build and story evidence.
findings.next_action: Use a direct Release Clinic link. Keep essential release metadata and actionable failures in the overview.

findings.observation: Work items show test counts. Build cards show repository, branch, status icons, and three coverage percentages.
findings.consequence: Build identity and comparison evidence receive less prominence than coverage values.
findings.next_action: Show pipeline and build identity with four commit references. Place coverage beneath comparison results.

findings.observation: A branch popover contains PROD, main, latest-commit, and PROD-to-main check results.
findings.consequence: Important comparison reasons require opening a small status control.
findings.next_action: Keep failed comparisons visible. Show four labeled commit hashes and explicit comparison directions per repository.

findings.observation: The screenshots show red zero coverage values and an ideal branch model.
findings.consequence: Screenshots alone cannot establish measurement availability, thresholds, or approved branching policy.
findings.next_action: Distinguish unavailable coverage from measured zero. Retain policy claims as source UI text until supported.

recommended_information_architecture.weekly_board: Chronological release cards retain the coming-week planning context.
recommended_information_architecture.compliance: Use a direct Release Clinic action in the release header. Do not duplicate its audit card grid.
recommended_information_architecture.evidence: Use a closed supporting-evidence section or secondary action. It needs no primary navigation tab.
recommended_information_architecture.overview: Show release identity, planned time, workflow state, failed reasons, and links to affected sections.
recommended_information_architecture.builds: Show repository, pipeline, candidate build, execution result, and the four references before coverage.
recommended_information_architecture.comparisons: Name both compared references. Show source counts and plain-language reasons with failed results first.
recommended_information_architecture.stories: Retain story identity, business title, workflow state, test results, and associated defects.

prototype_design_recommendations: Prefer one detail navigation system. Avoid separate tabs for compliance and evidence.
Use four reference cells or rows. Do not draw an ancestry graph without exact graph evidence.
Expose a failed reason directly. Keep successful detail and long commit lists expandable.
Use workflow state separately from automated check results and recorded human authorization.
Show source timestamps beside mutable branch references. Never imply current freshness from a saved snapshot.
Use color with text labels. Keep important actions available without hover.
Do not expand PT without a canonical definition. Its meaning does not block layout discussion.

confidence.rationale: The screenshots and user request support the hierarchy. No task-based usability study was performed.

material_limits: The photographs do not expose the four commit hashes themselves.
The ideal branch model is observed UI content. It does not establish approved business policy.
PT meaning and approval policy were not inferred.
No runtime behavior, source freshness, or service endpoint was tested.
limitations: Automated checks do not check the complete approved dictionary or grammar rules.
